clue.text: New writer's boat brought back water container

parts.note: the writer's is the setter talking of himself: I'm, written IM

indicators.note: brought back says the word for the boat is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a kind of boat

explanation.surface: Someone sails a new boat home carrying a water tank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns SUB into BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a rain cloud, so in a playful sense it holds water ready to fall.

clue.text: Distinguished, not forgotten, like some cakes

indicators.note: forgotten says the following word is dropped from the longer word, left out of mind

parts.note: to distinguish something is to notice it, so distinguished can mean noticed

explanation.surface: A baker's cakes stand out and are remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not forgotten' looks like 'remembered', but it tells you to take the letters NOT out of NOTICED.
explanation.definitionFit: Many cakes are finished with a sugary topping, so they are described as covered in icing.

clue.text: Study of pressure, except on old Metropolitan Line

parts.note: bar can mean except, as in 'all bar one'
Met is the short name for the Metropolitan (police, opera, line)
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Someone is researching pressure, but not on the old Metropolitan Line of the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Metropolitan Line is a London Underground line, but it is split up: Metropolitan and Line give separate pieces, with railway for line.
explanation.definitionFit: Barometry is the science of measuring air pressure, the work done with a barometer.

clue.text: Sparks off jumper perhaps, not mobile

definitions.meaning: ... electricity crackles from a woollen sweater pulled over the head

explanation.surface: A sweater crackles with sparks and someone stays put.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Static is both the charge built up by friction and the adjective for something stationary.

clue.text: A memo about time I had invested in cure

indicators.note: about says the memo goes round the other letters
invested in means placed inside, as money is put into a firm

parts.note: a memo is a short note
I had shortens to I'd, written ID

explanation.surface: A memo records time and money put into finding a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'invested in' both say TID goes inside A NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a remedy that counteracts a poison, so a cure in that sense.

clue.text: Complex opens with a traumatic 'Much Ado About Nothing'

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters that follow are mixed up

explanation.surface: A production of Shakespeare's comedy begins with a harrowing scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' looks like a noun or adjective of psychology, but it is the anagram signal for OPENS A TRAUMATIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm in a teacup is a fuss over something trivial, which is what much ado about nothing describes.

clue.text: How 1 might look beneath your blankets?

indicators.note: blankets as a verb means covers or wraps round, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: thy is the old form of your
under means beneath

explanation.surface: Someone asks how a figure would look hidden under your bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 is NIMBUS, a rain cloud. 'blankets' looks like bedding but is the verb for covering round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark nimbus cloud threatens a storm, so it looks as if thunder is coming.

clue.text: Party keeps Independent dry as before

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the party word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a do is a party
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol, so dry

explanation.surface: A political party keeps this newspaper alcohol-free just as it always has.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is short for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the same again, used to repeat what was said above or before.

clue.text: Rapidly falling hire charge stops bespoke tailor

indicators.note: stops as in plugs a gap, so the charge is placed inside
bespoke means made to order, so the letters of the next word are refashioned

parts.note: rent is the charge for hiring something

explanation.surface: A tailor making clothes to order is stopped by rent he owes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bespoke' rearranges the tailor's letters into TORIAL, and 'stops' plugs the charge into that.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrential rain pours down fast and heavily, as a torrent of water would.

clue.text: Area in warmest region of SW Asia

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: in the hide-and-seek game, warmest means nearest the target

explanation.surface: The hottest spot in southwest Asia is being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warmest' is the children's game sense: you get warmer as you near the hidden thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East is an older name for the lands of southwest Asia around the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Appear to swap parts for rally

indicators.note: swapping the two halves of the phrase moves the front word to the back

parts.note: to turn up is to appear or arrive

explanation.surface: Someone appears and changes roles at a political rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swap parts' puts UP before TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is an improvement or recovery, as a market rallies after a fall.

clue.text: Tried hot meal set out — by him?

definitions.text: Tried hot meal set out — by him?

indicators.note: set out means laid out afresh, so the letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether the hot meal set before them was laid out by the head waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: Semi-&lit: the anagram gives the answer, and the whole clue hints at the man who sets out meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A maître d'hôtel is the head waiter who runs a restaurant's dining room and sees meals served.

clue.text: Jolly troops twice quelling trouble like round trip

parts.note: a jolly is a party or outing, a do

indicators.note: quelling means suppressing, holding the trouble word down inside
twice says the troops letters are given two times

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means troops
a to-do is a fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A jolly outing for troops twice quelling trouble, like a round trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' makes OROR and 'quelling' puts TODO between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: A round, such as a milkman's, goes from house to house, hence door-to-door.

clue.text: Dash off a lot of material

definitions.meaning: a roll of cloth as it comes from the loom

explanation.definitionFit: Bolt means both to flee in a hurry and a whole roll of fabric.

clue.text: Bug Irish judge hosting Italian

indicators.note: hosting means having as a guest inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: An Irish judge has an Italian guest who is pestering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like an insect, but it is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to annoy them, which is what irritate means.

clue.text: Mild or medium note

parts.note: tempera is a painting medium bound with egg
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a sound is soft or middling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medium' looks like a size, but it is an artist's medium, a type of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperate climate is mild, free of extremes of heat or cold.

clue.text: Regularly torture depressed Palace fan?

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here the first, third, fifth and seventh

parts.note: blue means sad or depressed

explanation.surface: A gloomy football supporter suffers constant torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Palace' suggests Crystal Palace football club, but it is Buckingham Palace: a fan of the royals.
explanation.definitionFit: True-blue means staunchly loyal, as a devoted supporter of the royal family would be.

clue.text: Unresolved issue, such as 1?

definitions.meaning: a matter that is unclear or undecided
1 is NIMBUS, a dark rain cloud, so a patch of grey in the sky

explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is an ambiguous question, and literally a rain cloud is a grey area of sky.

clue.text: Intend miserly staff to maintain English average

definitions.meaning: to mean something is to intend it
the mean is the arithmetical average

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or keep, so the staff word keeps the letter inside it

parts.note: to man is to staff, as a crew mans a ship

explanation.surface: A stingy boss plans to keep an English worker on average pay.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition and wordplay too: E inside MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean covers intend, stingy and the statistical average, three separate senses of one word.

clue.text: Bard's duke's orison needs translating

indicators.note: translating means turning into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prayer by Shakespeare's nobleman has to be rendered in another language.
explanation.walkthrough: An orison is an old word for a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino is the Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night; the Bard is Shakespeare.

clue.text: Where student is presumably heading, in part

definitions.meaning: a student aims to come away with some academic degree
... means partly, to a certain extent

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means partly, and read literally it names the qualification a student is working towards.

clue.text: Daisy, or what might be studying her?

definitions.meaning: if Daisy is a cow, an ox's eye might be looking at her

explanation.definitionFit: The oxeye daisy is a common wild flower, and Daisy is a stock name for a cow an ox might eye.

clue.text: Notice tin containing very little

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the tin symbol goes round the small amount

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
1G, one gram, is a very small weight, written with I for one

explanation.surface: A notice says a tin holds hardly anything.
explanation.walkthrough: One gram is 1G; the figure 1 is shown as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice is a board or sign displaying information.

clue.text: Weary Arsenal wingers from the north

parts.note: to weary someone is to bore them

indicators.note: wingers are the players on the outside, so the outer letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Tired Arsenal wide players come down from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; its wingers are its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Boreal means northern, from Boreas, the Greek north wind.

clue.text: Shorten ascent on a tor in Cornwall primarily due to the weather

indicators.note: shorten means cut the end off, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a climb is an ascent

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A hiker cuts short a climb up a Cornish tor because of the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hilltop, common on the moors of Cornwall and Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Climatic means relating to climate, the long-run pattern of weather.

clue.text: Band at university reported icy spell

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word sounds like the one entered

parts.note: a frieze is a decorative band along a wall
to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: A student band's gig was reportedly hit by cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians; it is a decorative strip on a wall, which sounds like FREEZE.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeze-up is a period of hard frost when water and ground stay frozen.

clue.text: A lot of old headphones save energy

indicators.note: save in the sense of keep or hold, so the headphones word holds the letter

parts.note: cans is slang for headphones
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Old headphones are being used to cut energy use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' looks like 'except' or 'conserve', but here the headphones keep E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceans of something is an informal way of saying plenty of it.
